propositions: A blocked writer encountering a lock timeout sees only a bare pid, not what operation holds the lock, making it impossible to safely determine if interruption is safe.
Compaction sweeps hold the store write lock across multiple tickets and are safe to interrupt (skipped sweep is a no-op; events stay live and next trigger re-folds).
Lock holder identification must use an ambient contextvars-based operation label that reaches _owner_stamp without modifying acquisition call sites in compact_txn.py.
The lock timestamp stamp must remain colon-free with an optional op=label field appended, preserving forward compatibility with older rebar versions.
LockTimeout errors must include remedy text for known interruptible operations like compact-sweep, stating it is safe to terminate.
Staleness and reclamation logic must remain label-blind and unaffected by the operation label field.
